I can't believe they're just going to let me go like this after everything I've done for the company over these past three years. It feels like they don’t care at all about my contributions or how much I’ve invested in building something here. When I think about what’s ahead, it just makes me angrier and more resentful. They should have given me a proper explanation, some kind of acknowledgment of my work. Instead, they treated me like I was nothing more than a number on a spreadsheet. It's disgusting how they handled this whole thing.

I feel like I’m being punished for something I didn’t do wrong. And now, when people try to comfort me or give me advice, it’s like they don’t even understand the depth of what happened. They just want to pat me on the back and tell me everything will be okay, but how can anything ever be okay after this? It’s not fair, and I’m not going to let them get away with treating me like this.

That must feel really tough, being let go without much recognition for your hard work. It sounds like it's hitting you on a lot of different levels. Have there been any specific moments or words from colleagues that stood out as particularly hurtful?

Of course they did something hurtful! One colleague actually said to me, "It’s just business," like my years here meant nothing at all. How can someone say that after seeing the work I’ve put in and the relationships I built? It was like a slap in the face. And another one tried to tell me it would be good for me to have a break from this job, as if being laid off is some kind of vacation. They clearly don’t get what’s going on inside my head.

Every time someone tries to offer platitudes or generic advice, I just want to scream at them that they have no idea how much this hurts. It feels like everyone around me is either clueless or part of the problem. How can anyone think it's okay for a company to treat its employees this way? They should be ashamed of themselves.

It sounds really tough dealing with those comments from your colleagues. Their words must have stung deeply. Have you found any small ways to cope or express how you feel, even if it’s just talking to someone who truly understands?

I’ve tried talking to a few people about this, but every time I do, they either dismiss my feelings or offer some useless advice that doesn’t address what really happened. It's like they’re not listening at all. One friend suggested I should be grateful for the severance package and move on, which just made me angrier because it feels like she’s telling me to forget about everything I’ve worked for.

I feel like no one truly understands how betrayed I am by this whole situation. My manager could have shown a bit of respect and given me more than a two-minute video call. But instead, they acted like I was just another number in their budget cuts. It’s not fair, and it feels like everyone is either part of the problem or clueless about how to help.

I keep thinking about all the times I went above and beyond for this company, and now they’re treating me like I don’t matter at all. How am I supposed to feel anything but angry and hurt?

It sounds really frustrating that your feelings aren't being fully acknowledged by those around you. Have there been any moments where someone did listen or offered a bit of understanding, no matter how small? Sometimes even a little recognition can make a difference.

There have been a couple of moments where people tried to understand, but they still didn’t get it right. One coworker actually asked me if I felt like my work was undervalued and acknowledged that the layoff process could be really tough on someone with my tenure here. But even then, she couldn't offer anything concrete or meaningful beyond a sympathetic ear.

Another friend suggested I should talk to HR about getting more clarity on why they let me go, but when I brought it up, HR just gave me some generic response that didn’t address any of the specific concerns I had. It felt like another slap in the face.

I keep thinking about all the times I stayed late, took on extra projects, and helped my team through tough deadlines. And now they’re treating me like I’m disposable. How am I supposed to feel anything but angry when no one seems to recognize or appreciate that? It’s not just about the job; it’s about feeling valued as a person.

It sounds really challenging dealing with those responses from HR and your colleagues. Having your hard work acknowledged would make such a difference. Have you considered reaching out to someone outside of work, maybe a family member or another friend who might understand better? Sometimes an outsider can offer a fresh perspective or more empathy.

I’ve tried talking to my sister about it, but even she just tells me to stay positive and look for new opportunities. She doesn’t get how deeply this has affected me. It’s not just about finding another job; it’s about the injustice of being treated like I don’t matter after giving so much.

Every time someone tries to offer advice or comfort, it feels like they’re trivializing what happened. They say things like “it’ll be okay” or “you’ll find something better,” but how can anything ever feel okay when you’ve been let go without any real explanation or acknowledgment of your contributions? It’s not just about the job; it’s about feeling valued and respected.

I keep thinking that if anyone truly understood, they would see how unfair this whole situation is. But everyone seems to either dismiss my feelings or offer generic platitudes that don’t address what I’m going through. It’s frustrating and isolating, like no one really gets it.

It must feel very isolating not having someone fully understand the depth of your experience. Have you found any small moments where you felt a bit better, even if just for a little while? Sometimes those tiny moments can add up and help ease some of the frustration.

I’ve tried to find moments where I feel a bit better, but it’s hard when everything feels so unjust. There was one evening when I went for a long walk and just let myself be angry and upset without holding back. It felt good to release some of that pent-up frustration, even if it didn’t solve anything.

Another time, I talked to an old mentor who listened more than anyone else has. He acknowledged how tough this must be and said he believed in my worth beyond what the company did or didn’t see. That moment was brief but meaningful because someone finally recognized me for who I am, not just my role at the company.

But even those moments are few and far between. Most of the time, it feels like everyone is either dismissive or clueless about how much this has hurt me. It’s hard to shake off that feeling of being undervalued when no one around you seems to truly understand what I’ve been through.

Those moments with your walk and talking to your mentor sound really valuable. Even brief acknowledgments can make a big difference in tough times. Have there been any activities or hobbies outside of work that help you feel more grounded or centered?

I used to enjoy hiking and reading, but since the layoff, I haven’t found much joy in those things anymore. It feels like everything is tainted by this sense of betrayal and unfairness. Even when I try to engage in activities I once loved, it’s hard to escape the cloud of anger and resentment.

The thought of picking up a book or going for a hike just doesn’t feel right because my mind keeps circling back to what happened at work. It’s like this constant reminder that everything has changed, and nothing feels quite the same anymore. I keep thinking about all the times I looked forward to those activities as a break from work stress, but now they don’t offer the same comfort or escape.

It’s frustrating because I know these things used to help me feel better, but right now, it’s like there’s an emotional barrier that prevents me from finding any solace in them. Every time I try, my mind goes back to the injustice of being let go without proper recognition or explanation.

It sounds really tough that those activities aren’t providing the same comfort they used to. Sometimes giving yourself a bit of space and time can help. Have you tried doing something new or different to see if it shifts your perspective even slightly? Even small changes might make a difference.

I’ve thought about trying something new, but every idea feels tainted by this sense of injustice. It’s hard to muster the energy to start anything fresh when I’m so consumed with anger and frustration. The thought of putting effort into a new activity just doesn’t feel worth it right now.

Even if I try something different, like maybe taking up painting or joining a community group, I worry that my mind will keep drifting back to what happened at work. It feels like no matter what I do, the layoff is going to overshadow everything else in my life for a while.

I know logically that eventually things might get better, but emotionally, it’s difficult to see past this immediate pain and anger. Every time someone suggests doing something new or different, it just reinforces how much I’m struggling with this current situation. It feels like everyone is trying to push me forward before I’ve had a chance to process what happened.

So while I understand that trying something new might help eventually, right now it’s hard to even consider it. The pain and resentment are too raw, and everything feels clouded by this sense of unfairness.

It makes sense that you’re feeling overwhelmed and not ready for big changes just yet. Taking things one small step at a time can be helpful. Maybe starting with something very simple, like a short walk or a brief moment to yourself each day, could provide some relief without adding too much pressure. What do you think?

I appreciate the suggestion, but even those small steps feel daunting right now. The idea of going for a short walk or taking a few minutes to myself feels trivial compared to what I’m going through. It’s hard to see how something so minor could make a difference when everything else feels so big and overwhelming.

Every time someone suggests doing something simple, it just makes me feel more frustrated because those little things don’t seem like they can address the depth of my feelings. The pain and anger are so intense that I struggle to believe anything small will help.

I know logically that taking tiny steps might be better than doing nothing at all, but emotionally, it’s hard to find any motivation or hope in such minor actions. It feels like I need something more substantial to ease this sense of betrayal and injustice.

So while I understand the idea behind starting with small steps, right now, even those feel too insignificant to make a difference. The pain is just too raw, and everything seems so unfair that it’s difficult to see past that.

It sounds really tough to find motivation in such small steps when you’re feeling this way. It’s okay if those little things don’t seem significant right now. Maybe allowing yourself some time to just be with your feelings without pushing for immediate change could help. How do you feel about just sitting quietly or journaling for a few minutes each day?

Just the thought of sitting quietly or journaling feels like it might not be enough to address what I’m going through. It’s hard to believe that something as simple as writing down my thoughts or being alone for a few minutes could make any real difference when everything else feels so deeply unfair and hurtful.

I know that processing my feelings is important, but right now, even those small acts feel trivial compared to the weight of what happened at work. It’s frustrating because I can see how journaling might be helpful in theory, but emotionally, it doesn’t seem like it will make a dent in the anger and resentment I’m feeling.

Every time someone suggests something like this, it just reinforces how much I’m struggling and how little those suggestions feel like they understand my situation. It’s hard to find any comfort or relief in such minor actions when everything else feels so significant and unresolved.

So while I appreciate the suggestion, right now, even journaling or sitting quietly doesn’t seem like it will be enough to ease this pain. The injustice is just too raw, and it’s difficult to see past that.

It sounds really challenging to find comfort in those small actions when everything feels so significant. It’s okay if they don’t feel substantial right now. Maybe allowing yourself some time to just acknowledge how you’re feeling without the pressure of finding immediate relief could be helpful. Acknowledging my emotions feels like a start, but it’s still hard to see how that will make a real difference right now. Every time I try to sit with my feelings, the anger and resentment are so overwhelming that it’s difficult to believe anything can ease them.

I know that just acknowledging what I’m going through is important, but it feels like a Band-Aid on a deep wound. The pain and frustration are so intense that even recognizing them doesn’t seem sufficient. It’s frustrating because I want to feel better, but everything around me seems dismissive or inadequate in addressing the depth of my feelings.

So while acknowledging my emotions might be a step forward, it’s hard to believe that it will provide any real relief when everything else feels so unjust and unresolved. The betrayal and unfairness are just too raw, and it’s difficult to see past that pain.

Allowing my emotions to come and go feels like a step in the right direction, but it’s still hard to believe that it will make much of a difference. The anger and resentment are so intense that just letting them surface doesn’t seem like enough to ease the pain.

It sounds really tough to find much comfort in those moments when everything feels so overwhelming. Just allowing yourself to feel without judgment might help ease some of the intensity over time. How do you feel about trying to be gentle with yourself as these emotions come and go?

Being gentle with myself sounds like a good idea, but it’s hard to practice that gentleness when I’m so consumed by anger and resentment. The thought of being kind to myself in the face of this injustice feels almost impossible right now.

I know that treating myself with compassion might help eventually, but every time I try, it just highlights how much pain and frustration I’m feeling. It’s difficult to be gentle when everything around me seems so dismissive or inadequate in addressing what happened.

So while I understand the importance of being kind to myself, right now, it feels like a luxury I can’t afford. The betrayal and unfairness are too raw, and it’s hard to find any comfort in such small gestures when everything else feels so significant and unresolved.

It makes sense that being gentle with yourself feels challenging right now. Just acknowledging that you’re doing the best you can under these circumstances might help a little. How do you feel about giving yourself small moments of kindness, even if they don’t completely ease your pain?

Giving myself small moments of kindness feels like it could be helpful, but it’s still hard to believe that such small gestures will make much difference right now. The anger and resentment are so intense that even trying to be gentle with myself seems trivial compared to the depth of my feelings.

I know that acknowledging I’m doing the best I can is important, but every time I try, it just highlights how much pain and frustration I’m going through. It’s difficult to find any comfort in small acts of kindness when everything else feels so unfair and unresolved.

So while I understand the value of being kind to myself, right now, it feels like a minor comfort that won’t address the core issues.
